title: Fate Writing
next_chapter_hook: Chen Ji felt a bone-piercing chill as his Heavenly Fate drained away, as if some invisible force was siphoning his very life essence from within.

text.content: Those deep pupils were like an abyss, now suddenly blazing bright, transforming into two suspended scorching suns. It had no face, no form, yet radiated a pressure that overlooked all living beings, as if Heaven's Way itself was gazing upon ants. 'Fate Writer,' the voice echoed within Chen Ji's Mental Sea, 'Do you know why none of the previous holders of the Tianji Record dared to touch this forbidden art?' Chen Ji only felt his Mental Sea quaking—the voice did not come from outside, but was seared directly into his soul's depths. The golden runes on the fragment began to tremble violently, as if trying to break free of their restraints.

Chen Ji suppressed the agitation in his heart, a faint smile curling his lips: 'The predecessor specifically mentions it at this moment, surely means to tell this junior.' The voice fell silent for a moment, then let out a low laugh, tinged with admiration: 'Bold spirit. Heavenly Fate is the foundation of a mortal's lifespan and fortune. And the Fate Writer needs to use their own Heavenly Fate as ink, to write words that become reality.' Before the words finished, a mysterious rune shot out from that ancient eye, directly entering Chen Ji's Brow Center.

In an instant, Chen Ji's soul shook violently, unprecedented knowledge flooded his Mental Sea like a flood—a complete system of runes, each rune representing the power to rewrite fate. He saw countless possibilities: some used this art to reverse life and death, some to destroy dynasties, others even attempted to use it against Heaven's Way... and then they all died. 'The price,' the voice said coldly, 'For every word written, burn one year of Heavenly Fate. How much you want to change, how much you burn.'

Chen Ji shuddered throughout his body. One year of Heavenly Fate! He barely had less than a hundred years of life remaining, and if he wanted to rewrite something significant, it would cost decades or even a hundred years of burning. He instinctively checked his Heavenly Fate value—that column of numbers coldly glaring: 317 points. Each point represented one day, three hundred and seventeen days, not even a full year! 'With your current Heavenly Fate,' the voice seemed to see through his thoughts, 'You can write at most three hundred and seventeen characters. Changing something small is still possible, if you want to rewrite life and death... Hmph.'

dialogue.content: 'Three hundred and seventeen characters,' Chen Ji murmured, his brow tightly furrowed. He thought of the death prophecy in Chapter 700, the piercing pain of that arrow through his heart still seemingly echoing in his chest. To completely rewrite that ending, the characters needed would surely far exceed three hundred and seventeen. 'Predecessor,' he suddenly spoke, 'If there's a method to quickly increase Heavenly Fate, this junior is willing to pay any price.' The ancient existence fell silent, this silence lasting exceptionally long.

text.content: 'Any price?' The voice carried a hint of playfulness. Chen Ji nodded without hesitation, his eyes burning with obsession. He had been setting up this situation for so long, watching the chess game about to be completed, only to die in Chapter 700—he absolutely refused to be resigned. 'Very well.' The voice sighed, 'I originally didn't want you to know this art too early, after all, all previous masters of the Tianji Record died from their greed for the Fate Writer. But since you've come this far...' Those ancient eyes slowly closed, the runes glowing once more. This time, what emerged wasn't knowledge, but a blurry scene—a secluded place, a dry well, something seemed sealed within.

'Heavenly Fate Spring.' The voice whispered, 'In ancient times, it was the forbidden land set up by Heaven's Way to reward prophets. Drinking its water can extend lifespan or replenish Heavenly Fate. But this spring only opens once every hundred years, and it only recognizes...' It paused, 'Only recognizes the master of the Tianji Record.' Chen Ji stared intently at that scene, carving every detail into his mind. The well's location, the surrounding terrain, the faintly visible formation rune patterns... He had a premonition this might be the only chance. 'Once every hundred years?' He frowned, 'When was the last time it opened?'

'Fifty-seven years ago.' The voice replied calmly, 'In other words, you still have forty-three years.' Chen Ji's heart sank. Forty-three years... The death in Chapter 700 happened three years later, he couldn't possibly wait until then. Unless—'Unless you can find another path.' The voice seemed to see through his thoughts, 'For example... write a transition using the Fate Writer.' Chen Ji's pupils sharply contracted. 'Transition?' 'You don't need to rewrite the ending all at once, just write a... possibility.' The voice slowly said, 'Turn death into severe injury, turn certain death into recovery after severe injury. This might only cost a few dozen points of Heavenly Fate.'

Chen Ji fell silent. He naturally understood the subtlety—it was like playing chess, no need to checkmate in one move, just advance half a step, forcing the opponent to reveal weaknesses. But the problem was, every word the Fate Writer wrote would become established fact. 'If I write 'severe injury,'' he slowly spoke, 'Will this severe injury definitely happen?' 'Not necessarily.' The voice said, 'What you write is possibility, how it ultimately plays out depends on all parties' maneuvering. But one thing is certain—' It paused, 'Every word you write will be detected by the Eye of Heaven's Way. It will follow this thread and find you.'

Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill. The Eye of Heaven's Way... the ultimate villain that would be revealed in Volume 8, had actually already appeared in his awareness at this moment. What did this mean? Was the will of the Tianji Pavilion warning him, or tempting him? He took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. 'Predecessor,' he spoke, 'This junior has one thing I don't understand. Since the Tianji Pavilion is part of Heaven's Way, why teach this junior methods to oppose Heaven's Way?' The ancient existence fell silent, this silence lasting even longer. After a long while, it spoke: 'Because... I am not Heaven's Way.'

choice.prompt: The identity of the Tianji Pavilion's will is shrouded in mystery. How should you respond?

choices.description: Since the will of the Tianji Pavilion is not Heaven's Way, what exactly is it? Chen Ji decided to take a risk and ask.
choices.visible_cost: Might provoke the will of the Tianji Pavilion
choices.risk_hint: The will of the Tianji Pavilion might revoke the abilities just imparted

text.content: 'Not Heaven's Way? Then what exactly is the predecessor?' Chen Ji stared directly at those closed pupils, his voice calm yet carrying an unavoidable edge. The voice fell silent for a moment, then suddenly let out a desolate laugh: 'What am I... even I myself can no longer remember that question.' Those ancient eyes slowly opened, the pupils reflecting a chaotic starry sea. Chen Ji felt his Mental Sea violently quaking, as if some ancient memories were awakening.

choices.description: The identity of the Tianji Pavilion's will is too sensitive. Inquiring now might backfire. Better to first master the Fate Writer, and make calculations later.
choices.visible_cost: Miss the opportunity to understand the truth

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, forcibly suppressing that spark of curiosity. 'Since the predecessor is unwilling to say, this junior won't ask further.' He slightly bowed, his posture respectful yet unyielding, 'This junior only wishes to ask, how does one begin learning the Fate Writer?' The voice seemed somewhat surprised, then after a moment let out a light laugh: 'Quite composed indeed. Very well, since you already understand the price, follow me.' A door of light once again appeared in the void.

After the gate of light lay a void of darkness. Chen Ji felt as though he were adrift in an endless star sea, surrounded by infinite darkness, only those two eyes floating before him like an ancient lighthouse. "The first lesson of the Destiny Writer—" The voice was low and solemn, "is not to teach you how to write, but how not to write." Chen Ji was stunned. Not to write? "Countless masters of the Tianji Record all perished on the word 'write.'" The voice carried a hint of sorrow, "They believed they could rewrite everything, yet they did not realize that every act of writing exposed their location to the Eyes of Heavenly Dao."

Chills ran through Chen Ji's heart. He suddenly understood why every Tianji Record master throughout history met untimely deaths—not because of insufficient ability, but because of their greed. Every time they used the Destiny Writer, they were digging their own graves. "So," he said slowly, "this ability should never be used?" "Better yet, never use it at all," the voice said resolutely. "Unless..." It paused, "Unless you can accomplish one thing." Chen Ji pricked up his ears. "At the moment of writing, simultaneously erase your traces. Make the Eyes of Heavenly Dao see a non-existent being." The voice slowly said, "This is the purpose of the Heavenly Secrets Pavilion."

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. The Heavenly Secrets Pavilion... So the true purpose of this place was to conceal the traces of those who wielded the Tianji Record! What did this mean? Was the Pavilion's will protecting him or exploiting him? Just as he was about to ask, those two eyes suddenly blazed with dazzling light. "The first lesson ends." The voice suddenly turned cold, "Now comes the second lesson—writing." Before the words finished, a brush and paper appeared before Chen Ji out of thin air. The brush was jet black, like solidified night sky; the paper was blank, as if waiting to be filled with destiny.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stared at the floating brush, not reaching for it for a long while. He could sense the power contained within that brush—the power to rewrite life and death, yet also the power to destroy him. "What, scared?" The voice carried a hint of mockery. A slight smile curled at the corner of Chen Ji's mouth: "Fear is not the issue. I'm just wondering... how much Heavenly Fate does this brush require to activate?" He lifted his head, his gaze calm, "The junior wishes to know how much must be burned for the first trial."

text.content: The voice fell silent for a moment, then let out a low laugh: "Clever." Golden runes materialized in the void—showing Chen Ji's Heavenly Fate value: 317 points. "The first trial requires only one point." The voice said, "Write any character, and feel the sensation of Heavenly Fate burning. Remember, once this character falls, it becomes an established fact." Chen Ji took a deep breath, slowly extended his hand, and grasped the jet-black brush. The brush was ice-cold, feeling like holding frost, yet carried an eerie warmth, as if blood flowed within it.

choice.prompt: You have grasped the Brush of Destiny. What shall you write?

choices.description: Using his own name as the first attempt. Chen Ji wanted to see what kind of power his name could bear.
choices.visible_reward: Initial grasp of the sensation of the Destiny Writer

text.content: The brush tip touched the paper, and Chen Ji wrote his name—Ji. The moment the characters fell, a bone-deep chill spread from his fingertips throughout his body. He felt something within him being extracted, as if an invisible hand had seized his throat. In the next instant, the character "Ji" on the white paper suddenly glowed, transforming into a faint light that entered his chest. Strangely, he felt no discomfort; instead, he felt... several shades lighter.

choices.description: Sheng means both life and vitality. Chen Ji wanted to test whether this ability could affect life and death.
choices.visible_reward: Understanding the Destiny Writer's impact on life and death
choices.risk_hint: May attract the attention of the Eyes of Heavenly Dao
choices.process_label: test taboos, peer into life and death

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, his brush falling like a blade—"Sheng." The moment the characters fell, a powerful vitality burst from the paper, like spring wind brushing withered trees. He felt his Heavenly Fate value churning violently within, as if something had been awakened. "Interesting." The voice carried a hint of surprise, "You actually chose this character."

choices.description: Death, the opposite of destiny. Directly testing this ability's effect on death, even if only a sliver of possibility exists.
choices.visible_reward: Understanding the relationship between death and the Destiny Writer
choices.process_label: defy heaven, risk death for life

text.content: The brush tip hovered over the paper, and Chen Ji hesitated for a moment. Writing "Si"... This was the most dangerous choice, yet potentially the most valuable. Remembering the death prophecy from Chapter Seven Hundred, his heart hardened, and he wrote—"Si." The moment the character fell, the surrounding temperature dropped sharply, and those ancient eyes snapped wide open. "You—!" The voice carried a shocked tone for the first time. Chen Ji felt a cold, sinister energy surge into his body along the brush, as if something was watching him.

Chen Ji felt dizzy and disoriented, that icy energy coiling through his body like a poisonous snake. "Bold!" The voice roared, "Who told you to touch the character 'Si'!" Chen Ji bore the discomfort, a smile curling at his lips: "The junior merely... wished to know where the boundaries of this ability lie." He felt his Heavenly Fate value draining rapidly—not one point, but five! Just one "Si" character burned five points of Heavenly Fate! "Because of your probing, the Eyes of Heavenly Dao have noticed this place." The voice was ice-cold and biting, "You've landed yourself in serious trouble."

Chen Ji's heart tightened, but he did not panic. He felt that provoked existence rapidly approaching—a gaze beyond comprehension, as if the heavens themselves were gazing down upon an ant. "Senior," he said in a deep voice, "how should the junior deal with this?" The voice fell silent for a moment, then suddenly said: "You now have two choices." Chen Ji held his breath and listened intently. "First, leave the Tianji Pavilion immediately and abandon the inheritance of the Fate Writer." The voice said, "Second, stay, and endure the first gaze of the Heavenly Eye. Whichever choice you make, you have already been exposed."

choice.prompt: The Heavenly Eye is about to gaze upon this place. What is your choice?

choices.description: Since you have already been exposed, you might as well take this opportunity to see the true face of the Heavenly Eye. Danger and opportunity coexist.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence about the Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: The Heavenly Eye's gaze may cause permanent damage
choices.process_label: face heaven's might, win through danger

text.content: Chen Ji stood with hands behind his back, his gaze calm: "The junior will stay." The voice seemed somewhat surprised. After a moment, it let out a sigh: "You are... very well." Countless runes suddenly lit up in the void, weaving into a barrier that sheltered Chen Ji within. At the same time, a vast pressure descended from the heavens. Chen Ji felt his very soul trembling—the presence was something beyond recognition, its gaze like thorns in his back, as if it wished to strip away all his secrets.

choices.description: Preserve the青山 and there will be firewood. Protecting your life is the top priority.
choices.visible_cost: Lose the opportunity to understand the Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: May be tracked by the Heavenly Eye while fleeing

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate in the slightest, cupping his hands: "The junior takes his leave." Before his words finished, the pitch-black brush and that piece of paper suddenly turned into flowing light and merged into his brow center. At the same time, a teleportation rune lit up beneath his feet. "Remember," the voice urged, "the Fate Writer... never use it lightly! You already bear its mark within your body. The Heavenly Eye will eventually follow this thread to find you..." Brilliant light blazed. Chen Ji felt the world spinning, his consciousness instantly torn away.

When Chen Ji opened his eyes again, he had already returned to the small cottage in the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters. Outside the window, it was still deep night, moonlight filtering through the broken window lattice onto the ground. In his palm, that pitch-black brush flickered in and out of existence, as if it might dissipate at any moment. And in his mind, a complete inheritance had been added—the introductory cultivation method of the Fate Writer. But the cost was, his Heavenly Fate had plummeted from 317 points to 300. One impulsive attempt, costing a full seventeen points! Chen Ji lay on the bed, gazing at the ceiling, yet a cold smile curved his lips. Seventeen points exchanged for the truth—worth it. The death prophecy of Chapter Seven Hundred... he had finally seen the possibility of rewriting it.
